It takes A at {nu1PointBase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}, Cns, P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4}, the curve parameters a and b at {nu1ABase, 2 × u2ModLength + 8}, K at {nu1KBase} of u2KLength bytes and an uninitialized workspace of 8 × u2ModLength + 44 bytes. It uses the fast mode and fast reduction, so Cns must first be set up. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any of the pointers is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

GF2NEcConvProjToAffine converts a point A from projective to affine coordinates on a curve over GF(2^n): A, given in projective coordinates or as affine X and Y with Z = 1 at {nu1PointABase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}, is left with affine X and Y and Z set to 1. For the point at infinity the status is PUKCL_POINT_AT_INFINITY. It also takes Cns, P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4} and an uninitialized workspace of 4 × u2ModLength + 48 bytes. Cns must first be set up. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any of the pointers is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

GF2NEcConvAffineToProjective converts a point A from affine to projective coordinates on a curve over GF(2^n): A is given as affine X and Y with Z set to 1 and is left in projective (X, Y, Z) coordinates. It also takes Cns at {nu1CnsBase, u2ModLength + 8}, P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4} and an uninitialized workspace of 2 × u2ModLength + 16 bytes. Cns must first be set up. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails on the same alignment, Crypto RAM, length (under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4) and overlap faults as the other conversions.

GF2NEcRandomiseCoordinate replaces the projective coordinates (X1, Y1, Z1) of a point with another projective representation (X2, Y2, Z2) of the same point over GF(2^n), using a random number. The point at {nu1PointBase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12} must not be the point at infinity. It also takes Cns at {nu1CnsBase, u2ModLength + 8}, P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4}, the random number at {nu1RandomBase, u2ModLength + 4}, which is corrupted, and an uninitialized workspace of 3 × u2ModLength + 28 bytes. Cns must first be set up, and the hardware random number generator initialized, seeded and started. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any of the pointers is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

GF2NEcPointIsOnCurve tests whether a point, in projective coordinates and possibly the point at infinity, satisfies the curve equation over GF(2^n), and reports the answer in the status. It takes the point at {nu1PointBase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}, the curve parameters a and b at {nu1AParam} and {nu1BParam}, u2ModLength + 4 bytes each, Cns at {nu1CnsBase, u2ModLength + 8}, P and an uninitialized workspace of 4 × u2ModLength + 28 bytes. Cns must first be set up. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any of the pointers is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

GF2NEcDsaGenerateFast performs the second step of ECDSA signature generation to FIPS 186-2 over GF(2^n), in the same way as the GF(p) service: from a hash computed beforehand by any secure hash algorithm and a random scalar k, it computes (R, S). The hardware random number generator must be initialized, seeded and started, and k generated with it before the call. If k is outside [1, order - 1], or R or S comes out zero, it stops with PUKCL_WRONG_SELECT_NUMBER. Inputs: A in mixed coordinates (affine X, Y, Z = 1) at {nu1PointABase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}; an uninitialized Cns workspace; P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4}; an uninitialized workspace of 8 × u2ModLength + 44 bytes; the curve parameters a and b at {nu1ABBase, 2 × u2ModLength + 8}; and, each u2ScalarLength + 4 bytes, the order of A, k, the hash and the private key. u2ScalarLength is usually u2ModLength or u2ModLength + 4. The hash, of any SHA, may be no longer than the modulus and is zero-padded to u2ModLength + 4 bytes. The signature overwrites A: R and S each on u2ModLength + 4 bytes, zero-padded, followed by zeros in place of the third coordinate. It uses the fast mode and fast reduction. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any pointer is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

GF2NEcDsaVerifyFast performs the second step of ECDSA signature verification to FIPS 186-2 over GF(2^n): from the hash and the signature (R, S) it computes V and compares it with R, giving PUKCL_OK for a correct signature and PUKCL_WRONG_SIGNATURE for an incorrect one. The hardware random number generator must be initialized, seeded and started. Inputs: the base point A (affine X, Y, Z = 1) at {nu1PointABase, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}; an uninitialized Cns workspace at {nu1CnsBase, u2ScalarLength + 8}; P at {nu1ModBase, u2ModLength + 4}; an uninitialized workspace of 8 × u2ModLength + 44 bytes; the curve parameters a and b at {nu1ABase, 2 × u2ModLength + 8}; the order of A and the hash, each u2ScalarLength + 4 bytes; the public key (affine, Z = 1) at {nu1PointPublicKeyGen, 3 × u2ModLength + 12}; and the signature, stored like an affine point, at {nu1PointSignature, 2 × u2ScalarLength + 8}. The hash, of any SHA, may be no longer than the modulus and is zero-padded to u2ModLength + 4 bytes. A, the public key, the signature and the hash are corrupted. It uses the fast mode and fast reduction. No overlap between inputs and output is allowed. It fails if any pointer is not 32-bit aligned; if any area is not in Crypto RAM; if u2ModLength is under 12, over 0xffc or not a multiple of 4; or if any of the areas overlap.

The library runs its computations on the main core and shares resources with the application; it uses no global variables. Each service needs an estimated minimum of free stack; some options use less.

Timings are estimates at a 120 MHz CPU clock with the CPU and PUKCC at the same frequency, PUKCL data in Crypto RAM, test code and data in SRAM, and the instruction and data caches disabled; the values are approximate. RSA uses the ExpMod service (and CRT where stated); W is the window size. Prime generation uses PrimeGen. ECDSA over GF(p) signs with ZpEcDsaGenerateFast and verifies with ZpEcDsaQuickVerify; over GF(2^n) it signs with GF2NEcDsaGenerateFast and verifies with GF2NEcDsaVerifyFast.

The True Random Number Generator produces unpredictable random numbers from a physical entropy source rather than an algorithm, delivering a 32-bit number every 84 clock cycles. Its output passes the NIST SP 800-22 and Diehard random test suites, and it can serve as the entropy source for seeding a NIST-approved deterministic generator as FIPS PUB 140-2 and 140-3 require. It is built from an entropy source, control logic and an APB user interface clocked through MCLK, and signals the interrupt controller and the event system.

The TRNG has no I/O lines, DMA or analog connections. How it behaves in sleep depends on the sleep mode; its interrupt can wake the device, and its event can trigger other peripherals through the event system without leaving sleep. The bus clock CLK_TRNG_APB is gated in MCLK, its default state given in the peripheral clock masking. The interrupt line goes to the NVIC, which must be configured first. It is an event generator only, not an event user. It keeps running when the CPU is halted in debug, so a configuration that relies on the CPU servicing it may lose data then. All writable registers except INTFLAG can be write-protected by the PAC.

Once enabled, the TRNG delivers a new 32-bit random number in the DATA register every 84 CLK_TRNG_APB cycles, and can signal each one by interrupt or event. To use it: enable CLK_TRNG_APB with the TRNG bit of the MCLK APB mask register; optionally set EVCTRL.DATARDYEO for the output event and CTRLA.RUNSTDBY to run in Standby; then set CTRLA.ENABLE. Writing 0 to CTRLA.ENABLE disables it. EVCTRL is enable-protected and can only be written while CTRLA.ENABLE is 0.

One interrupt source, Data Ready (DATARDY), sets INTFLAG.DATARDY when a new number is in DATA; it is a synchronous wake-up source. It is enabled by writing 1 to INTENSET.DATARDY and disabled by writing 1 to INTENCLR. The request stays active until the flag is cleared or the interrupt disabled, and interrupts must also be enabled globally. The Data Ready output event is generated on each new number when EVCTRL.DATARDYEO is 1, and disabled by writing 0.

With CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 0 the TRNG stops in Standby but keeps its configuration; with RUNSTDBY = 1 it keeps running and any enabled interrupt can wake the CPU. The TRNG needs no register synchronization.

The device has two 12-bit successive-approximation ADCs, ADC0 and ADC1, each with its own sample-and-hold, so two inputs can be sampled at the same moment. Each converts at up to 1 Msps with 8-, 10- or 12-bit results, signed or unsigned, left- or right-adjusted. Each has up to 23 positive inputs (16 of them external pins, AIN[15..0]) and 8 negative inputs, measured single-ended or differentially. Internal inputs are the temperature sensors, the scaled core supply, the scaled I/O supply, the scaled VBAT supply and DAC0. The conversion range is VREF = 1.0 V to VDDANA, from an internal or an external reference. Conversions start from software or from an event, run once, continuously or in a DMA-driven sequence, and a window monitor compares results with thresholds. Hardware gain and offset correction, accumulation, averaging and oversampling with decimation (up to a 16-bit result), selectable sampling time and DMA transfer of results or settings are built in. While the Peripheral Touch Controller is enabled, ADC0 serves the PTC alone and is not available to the application.

The AIN and VREFA/VREFB/VREFC pins are configured through PORT as analog inputs. The ADC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs; all its interrupts except OVERRUN can wake the device, and its events can trigger other peripherals without waking it. Each ADC has a bus clock CLK_APB_ADCx, gated in MCLK, and needs its own generic clock GCLK_ADCx set up in GCLK before use; because these two clocks are asynchronous, some register writes are synchronized. Its DMA request line goes to the DMAC and its interrupt line to the NVIC, each configured first; its events go to the Event System. When the CPU halts in debug the ADC halts too, unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except INTFLAG can be write-protected by the PAC (not for an external debugger). An internal source used as input or reference (bandgap, DAC) must be configured and enabled before the ADC uses it.

Software must copy the BIASREFBUF, BIASR2R and BIASCOMP values, measured in production and kept in the NVM Software Calibration Area, into the ADC CALIB register; without them the ADC does not convert to its specified accuracy.

operation.topic: ADC enabling, resetting and starting conversions
operation.text: CTRLA (apart from ENABLE and SWRST), EVCTRL and CALIB are enable-protected: they can be written only while CTRLA.ENABLE is 0. Writing 1 to CTRLA.ENABLE turns the ADC on and 0 turns it off; writing 1 to CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and leaves the ADC disabled. The input is chosen in INPUTCTRL. A conversion starts when SWTRIG.START is written 1 or when an enabled event arrives; sampling begins only on that trigger, not when the multiplexer is set. In free-running mode the first conversion is started and each later one begins when the previous one ends. Each result overwrites RESULT; with more than one channel in use the result must be read as soon as INTFLAG.RESRDY is set, or INTFLAG.OVERRUN marks a lost result. The conversion rate is set by the GCLK_ADCx frequency and the ADC's internal prescaler, which divides by 2 to 256 in powers of two (CTRLA.PRESCALER, DIV2 minimum) to give CLK_ADCx.

operation.topic: ADC reference, resolution and input mode
operation.text: REFCTRL.REFSEL picks the reference, internal by default or external. CTRLB.RESSEL selects 8-, 10- or 12-bit results (12 by default); fewer bits shorten the conversion. Single-ended conversion gives the full 12 bits when the positive input is always positive; differential mode (INPUTCTRL.DIFFMODE = 1) is used when the positive input may fall below the negative one. Either can run as single conversions or free-running, with INTFLAG.RESRDY set at the end of each conversion.

After a software or event start is synchronized to GCLK_ADCx, the input is sampled in the first half period of CLK_ADC, then one bit is resolved per CLK_ADC cycle from MSB to LSB. SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN lengthens the sampling time. SAMPCTRL.OFFCOMP adds an offset-compensation phase before sampling; with it the sampling time must be one CLK_ADC cycle. Lower resolution raises the free-running rate. Example: 1 Msps at 12 bits with a four-cycle sampling time needs CLK_ADC = 1 Msps × (4 + 12) = 16 MHz, and since the prescaler divides by at least 2, GCLK_ADC = 32 MHz.

AVGCTRL.SAMPLENUM sets how many consecutive conversions are summed, 1 to 1024. Past 16 samples the sum would overflow the 16-bit RESULT, so it is shifted right automatically. Averaging divides the sum by the sample count: the automatic shift plus a further right shift written to AVGCTRL.ADJRES; it improves accuracy in noise at the cost of rate, and averaging SAMPLENUM samples divides the un-averaged sampling rate by SAMPLENUM. INTFLAG.RESRDY is set when the averaged result is ready. Accumulating or averaging two or more samples needs CTRLB.RESSEL set accordingly.

Oversampling raises the resolution from 12 up to 16 bits at a lower effective rate: for n extra bits, 4^n samples are summed and the sum shifted right by n, the shift split between the automatic shift and AVGCTRL.ADJRES.

The window monitor compares each RESULT with a lower threshold WINLT and an upper threshold WINUT, in the mode set by CTRLB.WINMODE, and sets INTFLAG.WINMON on a match. With CTRLB.WINSS = 1 it compares every single sample instead of the accumulated value and STATUS.WCC counts the matching samples; the flag is then set when that count is not zero. The thresholds are signed in differential mode and unsigned otherwise, and only as many low bits count as the selected resolution; in 8-bit differential mode the eighth bit is the sign even if the ninth is zero.

Offset error is the departure of the transfer function from the ideal line at zero input; gain error is the departure of the last step's midpoint from the ideal line once offset is removed. With CTRLB.CORREN set, the value in OFFSETCORR is subtracted from each conversion and the difference multiplied by GAINCORR before it is written to RESULT. Correction adds 13 CLK_ADC cycles of latency: only on the first conversion in free-running mode, on every conversion in single mode.

Two temperature sensors at different places on the die, TSENSP and TSENSC, controlled by the SUPC, give voltages VTP and VTC that the ADC can convert. When SUPC.VREF.ONDEMAND = 0, with SUPC.VREF.TSEN = 1 and SUPC.VREF.VREFOE = 0, SUPC.VREF.TSSEL chooses the sensor and the ADC input multiplexer settings make no difference. When SUPC.VREF.ONDEMAND = 1 and TSEN = 1, the sensor follows the one the ADC requests through INPUTCTRL.MUXPOS, regardless of TSSEL, and VREFOE may also be 1. The die temperature is computed from the two results TP and TC together with calibration constants stored in the NVM Software Calibration Area; accuracy depends on temperature and falls off towards the extremes.

The ADC is most accurate when the input common-mode voltage is near VREF/2. Setting CTRLA.R2R allows the full common-mode range; it needs a four-cycle sampling period, which offset compensation (SAMPCTRL.OFFCOMP = 1) provides, and is not to be used with offset compensation off.

INPUTCTRL, CTRLB, REFCTRL, AVGCTRL, SAMPCTRL, WINLT, WINUT, GAINCORR and OFFSETCORR are double buffered: a write goes to a buffer without disturbing the conversion in progress, sets the matching SYNCBUSY bit, and reaches the ADC when the next RESULT is ready and a new conversion can start.

The DMA controller can reload a set of ADC settings between conversions by writing DSEQDATA. Each register that takes part has an enable bit in DSEQCTRL; sequencing is on while any DSEQCTRL bit is 1, which sets DSEQSTAT.BUSY. It stops when the ADC is disabled or reset, when DSEQCTRL is written 0 and the current sequence ends, or when INPUTCTRL.DSEQSTOP is 1 and the current sequence ends, after one further measurement; BUSY then clears and no more DMA triggers are made. Writing DSEQCTRL non-zero clears DSEQSTOP. A stopped sequence restarts on writing DSEQSTOP to 0, on SWTRIG.FLUSH, or on a flush event with EVCTRL.FLUSHEI enabled. The DSEQ trigger is made while BUSY is 1, the ADC is idle or starting a conversion and a register group is still pending; DSEQSTAT holds the groups still to be written and is refilled from DSEQCTRL (except AUTOSTART) when it empties, starting a new sequence at the next conversion. Only 32-bit DMA writes to DSEQDATA are accepted; a register not enabled ignores its part of the word.

operation.topic: ADC DMA sequencing descriptor and memory layout
operation.text: For sequencing the DMA channel uses word beats (BTCTRL.BEATSIZE = WORD), source increment by one step (SRCINC = 1, STEPSEL = SRC, STEPSIZE = X1), no destination increment, a block count in BTCNT, a source address in SRCADDR, ADC.DSEQDATA as the destination, single-beat bursts (CHCTRLA.BURSTLEN = SINGLE), burst trigger action (TRIGACT = BURST) and the ADC DSEQ trigger as source (TRIGSRC = DSEQ), then optional channel interrupts and the channel enable. Each enabled register group takes one 32-bit word, packed one after another in memory in the order INPUTCTRL/CTRLB, REFCTRL/AVGCTRL/SAMPCTRL (byte 1 unused), WINLT/WINUT, GAINCORR/OFFSETCORR; a group not in the sequence takes no word. With DSEQCTRL.AUTOSTART = 1 a new conversion starts by itself when a sequence completes, once any averaging or oversampling has delivered its RESULT. Free-running mode (CTRLB.FREERUN = 1) cannot be used with sequencing, and an event start (EVCTRL.STARTEI = 1) disables AUTOSTART.

Writing ADC1.CTRLA.SLAVEEN = 1 makes ADC1 a client of ADC0: GCLK_ADC0 and ADC0's controls are routed to ADC1, ADC1 is enabled through ADC0's CTRLA, and ADC0's event inputs drive both, so input events are configured in ADC0.EVCTRL. For DMA sequencing on ADC1 in this mode, ADC0 is enabled first (ADC0.CTRLA.ENABLE = 1), then ADC1.DSEQCTRL written non-zero. ADC0.CTRLA.DUALSEL chooses whether one trigger starts both ADCs together or alternately (interleaved, ADC0 then ADC1 on successive triggers). Interleaving works only in single-conversion mode (CTRLB.FREERUN = 0); it is restarted by flushing ADC0 (ADC0.SWTRIG.FLUSH = 1), disabling and re-enabling ADC0, resetting and reconfiguring ADC0, or a flush event (EVCTRL.FLUSHEI = 1).

DMA requests: RESRDY, set when a result (or a finished average) is available and cleared when RESULT is read, and DSEQ for sequencing. Interrupts: RESRDY, WINMON and OVERRUN; all but OVERRUN are asynchronous wake-up sources. Each has a flag in INTFLAG, enabled by writing 1 to INTENSET and disabled by writing 1 to INTENCLR; a request lasts until its flag is cleared, the interrupt disabled or the ADC reset, and all are ORed into one NVIC request. Output events: RESRDY when a result is available and WINMON on a window match, each enabled by an EVCTRL.xxEO bit. Input events: START a conversion and FLUSH, each enabled by an EVCTRL.xxEI bit. The ADC uses asynchronous event paths only and reacts to a rising edge; EVCTRL.xINV inverts an input to act on the falling edge. Any of several connected events triggers the enabled action, and FLUSH wins when FLUSH and START arrive together.

CTRLA.RUNSTDBY and CTRLA.ONDEMAND set what an enabled ADC does in Standby. With ONDEMAND = 1 the analog block powers down after each conversion; a start request wakes it and the conversion begins after the start-up time.
Writes to CTRLA.SWRST and CTRLA.ENABLE are synchronized, as are writes to INPUTCTRL, CTRLB, REFCTRL, AVGCTRL, SAMPCTRL, WINLT, WINUT, GAINCORR, OFFSETCORR and SWTRIG.

The Analog Comparator peripheral holds one pair of comparators, COMP0 and COMP1, alike but separately controlled. Each compares its positive and negative input and gives a digital output, 1 when the positive input is higher. The pair can be joined in window mode to test a signal against a voltage range. Hysteresis is selectable (off, or three levels on). Inputs are four shared pins, AIN0 to AIN3, usable as positive or negative inputs, plus ground (for zero crossing), the bandgap reference, a 64-level VDDANA scaler per comparator and DAC0. Interrupts can come on a rising or falling edge, a toggle or the end of a comparison, and in window mode on the signal going above, inside, below or outside the window. Events are made from the comparator outputs and the window inside/outside state. Each output can drive a pin, raw or synchronized, and an optional digital filter cleans the output.

AC pins are configured through PORT, analog pins with their digital input and output disabled. The AC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs, its interrupts can wake the device and its events reach other peripherals without waking it. The bus clock CLK_AC_APB is gated in MCLK; the generic clock GCLK_AC must be set up in GCLK first and is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some writes are synchronized. The AC has no DMA. Its interrupt lines go to the NVIC and its events to the Event System. In debug halt it stops after any comparison in progress unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except CTRLB and INTFLAG can be write-protected by the PAC. Both comparators of the pair use one common set of four pins. Internal sources (bandgap, DAC) must be configured and enabled before use as inputs. For specified accuracy, software copies the BIAS value (measured in production, kept in the NVM Software Calibration Area) into the AC CALIB register.

EVCTRL is enable-protected. CTRLA.ENABLE turns the AC on and off; CTRLA.SWRST resets all registers and disables it. Each comparator is set up in its COMPCTRLx before it is enabled and cannot be changed while enabled: measurement mode (SINGLE), hysteresis (HYSTEN, HYST), interrupt source (INTSEL), inputs (MUXPOS, MUXNEG), filter (FLEN) and standby operation (RUNSTDBY). COMPCTRLx.ENABLE turns one comparator on or off; clearing CTRLA.ENABLE stops all comparators without clearing their ENABLE bits.

After a comparator is enabled, an automatically measured start-up time passes before its first result, and its output is unavailable meanwhile. Interrupts can be set for toggle, rising edge, falling edge or end of comparison; events follow the output whether or not an interrupt is enabled. In continuous mode (SINGLE = 0) comparisons run without pause, STATUSA.STATEx always holds the latest result, and STATUSB.READYx is set after the first; edges are found by comparing successive samples taken at the GCLK_AC rate. In sleep a continuous comparator can run without a clock: a change is detected asynchronously, GCLK_AC is started to log the event or interrupt and stopped again unless the device is to wake. In single-shot mode (SINGLE = 1) the comparator idles until CTRLB.STARTx is written 1 (which also clears READYx) or an event arrives with EVCTRL.COMPEIx set (which leaves READYx alone); after the start-up time one comparison is made and READYx is set. Event-triggered single shots work in sleep: GCLK_AC is started for the comparison and stopped again afterwards unless the device is to wake.

The positive input (COMPCTRLx.MUXPOS) is one of the AIN pins; the negative input (COMPCTRLx.MUXNEG) is an AIN pin or one of the internal references shared by the comparators. A pin used as an input has its digital input and output disabled in PORT. The multiplexers switch so as to keep crosstalk between channels low, and the input selection is changed only while the comparator is disabled. For the CCL to use the comparison results internally, the field is set to 0x1 or 0x2.

WINCTRL.WENx joins a comparator pair into a window comparator: both take the same pin as positive input and their negative inputs set the upper and lower limits, either way round. Both comparators must have the same SINGLE setting and the same RUNSTDBY setting. Both are enabled before WINCTRL.WEN0 is set, WEN0 is cleared before either is disabled, and both STATUSB.READYx are checked before results are read. STATUS.WSTATEx gives the window state. WINCTRL.WINTSEL picks an interrupt on the input going below, above, into or out of the window; window events follow the inside/outside state whether or not the interrupt is enabled, and each comparator's own outputs, interrupts and events keep working. In single-shot window mode both comparators measure together, started by either CTRLB.STARTx bit or either event.

Each comparator has its own 64-level divider of the supply, giving a fraction of VDDANA as a reference. It is on while the comparator is enabled and VSCALE is chosen as its negative input (MUXNEG = 5) or positive input (MUXPOS = 4); SCALERx.VALUE (6 bits) sets the level.

COMPCTRLx.HYSTEN turns hysteresis on for one comparator and COMPCTRLx.HYST sets its level; hysteresis works only in continuous mode. COMPCTRLx.FLEN selects no filter or a 3-sample or 5-sample majority filter sampled at the GCLK_AC rate: an output change counts once N/2+1 of the last N samples agree. Filtering delays the validated output by N−1 sampling cycles; in continuous mode later outputs follow every cycle, in single-shot mode the comparison ends after the Nth sample. In sleep, filtering works only for single-shot measurements and must be off for continuous measurements in sleep, or interrupts and events may be wrong.

COMPCTRLx.OUT routes a comparator's output to its CMP[x] pin, either raw and unsynchronized or synchronized to CLK_AC with filtering. COMPCTRLx.SWAP exchanges the positive and negative inputs and inverts the output, so the input offset can be measured or cancelled; the output inverts only while the input difference lies within the offset. SWAP is changed only while the comparator is disabled.

Interrupt sources: COMP0 and COMP1 on a change of comparator state as chosen by COMPCTRLx.INTSEL, and WIN0 on a change of window state as chosen by WINCTRL.WINTSEL[1:0]. Each has a flag in INTFLAG, enabled by writing 1 to INTENSET and disabled by writing 1 to INTENCLR; a request lasts until its flag is cleared, the interrupt disabled or the AC reset, and all are ORed into one NVIC request. Output events COMP0, COMP1 (a copy of the comparator state) and WIN0 (a copy of the window inside/outside state) are enabled by EVCTRL.xxEO bits. Input events START0 and START1, enabled by EVCTRL.COMPEIx, start a comparison after the start-up time; in window mode either event starts both comparators.

COMPCTRLx.RUNSTDBY sets each comparator's behaviour in Standby: at 0 it is off in sleep, its analog part powered down, keeping its configuration and needing the start-up time on return; at 1 it keeps running and any enabled AC interrupt can wake the CPU. Both comparators of a window pair need the same RUNSTDBY. The AC also works in sleep modes where its clock is stopped, as long as it stays powered (not in shutdown). A continuous comparator then runs asynchronously, starting GCLK_AC only to log a matching edge, and can wake the device if its interrupt is enabled; filtering is not possible this way. A single-shot comparator is started by an input event, GCLK_AC runs for the comparison (filtering allowed) and both stop again unless the device is to wake.
Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, COMPCTRLn.ENABLE and the WINCTRL register are synchronized.

The DAC controller drives two 12-bit DACs, DAC0 and DAC1, used as two independent outputs or together as one differential DAC. Each converts at up to 1 Msps. Each has an interpolation filter with 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x or 32x oversampling, usable in line with its DAC or on its own, and dithering gives 16-bit resolution in hardware. Conversions start from software, DMA or events. The outputs have high drive, DAC0's output is also an internal input to the AC and ADC, and DMA is supported.

VOUT0, VOUT1 and VREFA are configured through PORT before use, and an internal input is enabled before the DAC controller. The DAC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs, its interrupts can wake the device and its events reach other peripherals without waking it. The bus clock CLK_DAC_APB is gated in MCLK; the generic clock GCLK_DAC must be set up in GCLK first and is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some writes are synchronized. Its DMA request lines go to the DMAC and its interrupt line to the NVIC, each configured first; its events go to the Event System. In debug halt it stops after finishing any conversion, unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except INTFLAG and DATABUFx can be write-protected by the PAC. The analog signals of the AC, ADC and DAC can be connected together.

Each DAC turns the value in its data register (DATA0, DATA1) into a voltage on its output (VOUT0, VOUT1); a conversion starts when new data is loaded or on an input event. CTRLB, EVCTRL, DACCTRL0 and DACCTRL1 are enable-protected. CTRLA.ENABLE turns the controller on and off; CTRLA.SWRST resets all registers and disables it. Each DAC is set up in its DACCTRLx, applied when the controller is enabled: ENABLE; LEFTADJ (1 left-aligns data in bits [31:20], 0 right-aligns it in [11:0]); RUNSTDBY (1 keeps converting in Standby, 0 halts the DAC there); DITHER; REFRESH[3:0] (a value above 1 turns on refresh); CCTRL[1:0], the output buffer current, chosen by data rate for low power; FEXT (1 uses the filter standalone, 0 in line with the DAC); and OSR[2:0] (0 no oversampling, other values interpolate). After enabling, each DAC needs a start-up time; STATUS.READYx = 1 shows it is ready and conversions started before then are discarded. VOUTx is tri-stated while its DAC is disabled.

The output spans GND to the reference chosen by CTRLB.REFSEL: the internal VREF (default), VDDANA or the external VREFA. DATAx is loaded by a CPU write, by DMA, or from DATABUFx on a STARTx event, and each DAC starts its conversions independently even on a shared GCLK. A conversion takes 24 GCLK_DAC periods, after which STATUS.EOCx = 1 shows VOUTx is stable; being pipelined, a new conversion can begin every 12 periods, and data written during a conversion waits for the next slot.
The DAC reference must be below VDDANA. The maximum rate of 1 Msps is reached only with VDDANA above 2.4 V. GCLK_DAC must be 12 MHz or lower, which corresponds to 1 Msps.

In single mode (CTRLB.DIFF = 0) the DMA requests are EMPTY0 and EMPTY1, set when data moves from DATABUFx or DATAx into DACx's internal buffer and cleared by writing DATAx or DATABUFx or by clearing INTFLAG.EMPTYx, and RESRDY0 and RESRDY1, set when a standalone filter's output is ready and cleared through INTFLAG. In differential mode (CTRLB.DIFF = 1) only EMPTY0 is used, for the transfer into DAC1's buffer. CPU access to the registers that set or clear a DMA request can lose the request or corrupt the transfer. Interrupts: EMPTY0/1 (internal buffer empty), UNDERRUN0/1 (buffer empty when a start event came), RESRDY0/1 (standalone filter result ready) and OVERRUN0/1 (RESULTx got new data before the DMA request was cleared); all are asynchronous wake-up sources, enabled through INTENSET and INTENCLR and ORed into one NVIC request. Output events EMPTY0/1 and RESRDY0/1 are enabled by EVCTRL output bits. Input events START0/1, enabled by EVCTRL.STARTEIx, copy DATABUFx into DATAx when DACx is ready and start the conversion; they are resynchronized to GCLK_DAC, and with a start event enabled only DATABUFx is written. Events act on their rising edge by default; EVCTRL.INVEIx = 1 makes them act on the falling edge; any of several connected events triggers the action. An event arriving before the start-up time ends loads DATAx but starts no conversion.

With DACCTRLx.RUNSTDBY = 1 a DAC keeps converting in Standby, and an input event in sleep makes the controller request GCLK_DAC to finish the conversion (SleepWalking). With RUNSTDBY = 0 it stops and is powered down in Standby, and needs its start-up time again on wake-up. Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, DATA0, DATA1, DATABUF0 and DATABUF1 are synchronized. After changing GCLK PCHCTRLm.CHEN the bit is read back to confirm the synchronization has finished.
While DAC0 is enabled its output VOUT0 is available inside the device as an input to the AC and ADC; the VOUT0 pin is then given over to this and cannot take another function.

operation.topic: DAC output buffer current and refresh
operation.text: The output buffer current, chosen with DACCTRLx.CCTRL to suit the conversion rate, sets the power used. A DAC holds its output within one LSB for about 100 µs, so a static output or one updated below 20 kSPS needs periodic refresh: with DACCTRLx.REFRESH set, OSCULP32K restarts the conversion of DATAx after each refresh period unless a new conversion has started. REFRESH = 0 turns refresh off and 1 is reserved. The period follows the OSCULP32K tolerance. Refresh works only without interpolation (OSR = 0x0), stays on in Standby when RUNSTDBY = 1, and data written during a refresh conversion waits for the next slot.

With CTRLB.DIFF = 1 both DACs convert DATA0 together, giving an output balanced about VREF/2: VOUT0 is the positive side and VOUT1 the negative. DATA0 is then a signed two's-complement value with DATA0[11] as sign, range −2047 to 2047; 2047 puts VOUT0 at VREF and VOUT1 at 0, 0 puts both at VREF/2. DACCTRL0 configures both DACs and DACCTRL1 need not be written.

With DACCTRLx.DITHER = 1, DATAx is a 16-bit unsigned value: bits [15:4] are the 12-bit code and bits [3:0] the dither. Each 16-bit value is made as 16 sub-conversions of either DATAx[15:4] or DATAx[15:4] + 1, whose average equals the 16-bit value. The STARTx event must come 16 times per value and DATABUFx be loaded every 16 conversions, so EMPTYx events and DMA requests come every 16 transfers while STATUS.EOCx still marks each sub-conversion.

A non-zero DACCTRLx.OSR selects interpolation at 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x or 32x: input data is taken once every OSR trigger events and recomputed at the trigger rate by a third-order SINC filter; fs, the input sampling frequency, is the trigger frequency divided by OSR. With DACCTRLx.FEXT = 0 the filter feeds the DAC and RESULTx reads zero; with FEXT = 1 the DAC stays at zero and RESULTx holds the filter output, for a standalone filter served by DMA. Dithering and interpolation can run together when DITHER and OSR are both set before the DAC is enabled; the dithered output is then sampled over OSR events, and OSR must be 2, 4, 8 or 16.

The device has up to eight Timer/Counter instances. Each is a counter with a prescaler, two compare/capture channels and control logic, counting clock pulses or events. It runs as an 8-, 16- or 32-bit counter. Compare channels generate frequencies or single-slope PWM; capture channels timestamp events or pin edges and measure frequency, pulse width, period, and minimum or maximum values. The period setting (8-bit mode only) and the compare channels are double buffered. There is one input event; interrupts and output events come on overflow or underflow and on compare match or capture; DMA is supported.

TC pins are configured through PORT. A TC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs, its interrupts can wake the device and its events reach other peripherals without waking it. Each has a bus clock CLK_TCx_APB gated in MCLK and a generic clock GCLK_TCx asynchronous to it, so some register accesses are synchronized. Two TC instances can share one peripheral clock channel and then cannot run at different clock frequencies (see the GCLK PCHCTRLm mapping). DMA request lines go to the DMAC and the interrupt line to the NVIC, each configured first; events go to the Event System. In debug halt it stops unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except INTFLAG, STATUS, COUNT, PER, PERBUF, CCx and CCBUFx can be write-protected by the PAC. It has no analog connections.

Each TC has two compare/capture channels, CC0 and CC1. The counter counts GCLK_TCx ticks, optionally prescaled, or Event System events, and its value goes to the channels to be compared or captured. CCx and CCBUFx share hardware: after writing CCBUFx, the CCx register stays locked (SYNCBUSY.CCx = 1) until the buffer has been loaded into it; each buffer has a valid flag (BUFV) showing it holds a new value. COUNT, CCx and CCBUFx are 8, 16 or 32 bits wide as set by CTRLA.MODE; in 8-bit mode a period register PER and its buffer PERBUF are added. The counter range and clock set the finest time resolution. The TC counts up or down, comparing the count with TOP or ZERO and with each CCx; matches can raise DMA requests, interrupts or events and in waveform modes set period and pulse width. Capture measures period and pulse width or records edges from a pin or an event.

CTRLA (except ENABLE and SWRST), DRVCTRL, WAVE and EVCTRL are enable-protected; enable-protected CTRLA bits can be written in the same 32-bit access that sets ENABLE, but not in one that clears it. Before enabling: turn on CLK_TCx_APB; choose 8-, 16- or 32-bit mode in CTRLA.MODE (16-bit by default); choose a waveform mode in WAVE.WAVEGEN; optionally set CTRLA.PRESCALER and, with a prescaler, CTRLA.PRESYNC; optionally set one-shot (CTRLBSET.ONESHOT) and down-counting from TOP (CTRLBSET.DIR); for capture, enable channels in CTRLA.CAPTEN; optionally invert outputs or pin inputs with DRVCTRL.INVEN. CTRLA.ENABLE turns the TC on and off; CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL and should be used only with the TC disabled. The prescaler divides GCLK_TCx by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256 or 1024 (outputs from 1 to 1/1024); above 1, CTRLA.PRESYNC chooses whether the counter update happens on the next GCLK_TCx or the next prescaled clock. Event counting bypasses the prescaler. The combined prescaler and event-action tick stream is CLK_TCx_CNT.

CTRLA.MODE selects COUNT8, with its own PER and PERBUF registers; COUNT16, the default, without a separate period register; or COUNT32, made by pairing TC(2n) with TC(2n+1). A pair is configured through the even-numbered TC, both bus clocks must be on, and the odd partner becomes a client with STATUS.SLAVE set: its registers do not show the 32-bit counter, writing them has no effect on it, and normal access to its COUNT and CCx is not allowed.

Each CLK_TCx_CNT tick clears, reloads, increments or decrements the counter; a clear or reload ends one counter cycle and starts the next. CTRLB.DIR = 0 counts up, 1 counts down. Counting up from TOP it goes to zero on the next tick (overflow); counting down from ZERO it reloads TOP (underflow); either sets INTFLAG.OVF, which can trigger an event, interrupt or DMA transfer, and stops the counter when CTRLBSET.ONESHOT is set. COUNT can be written while running and the write takes priority over counting; a fresh start begins from ZERO or TOP unless COUNT was written or the TC stopped elsewhere. The direction can change while running. Settings take effect after synchronization, and the counter must be in normal operation when it is the time base for capture channels. A STOP command (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x2) stops the counter without keeping its value, clears all waveforms and sets STATUS.STOP. RETRIGGER (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x1, or EVCTRL.EVACT = 0x1) clears or reloads the running counter by direction, or resumes a stopped one from COUNT; with the retrigger event action set, enabling the TC does not start it, the next event does. EVCTRL.EVACT = 0x2 (COUNT) counts events up or down by direction, without PWM. EVCTRL.EVACT = 0x3 (START) starts a stopped counter on an event or a retrigger command and has no effect while counting.

Channels default to compare. The counter is compared continuously with each CCx, for timing or waveforms. CCBUFx double buffers CCx: the buffer is copied at UPDATE or on a forced update command (CTRLBSET.CMD = UPDATE), which keeps pulses symmetric and outputs glitch-free. For a waveform on a pin: choose WAVE.WAVEGEN, optionally invert WO[x] with DRVCTRL.INVENx, and configure the pin in PORT; events are not used on a channel in waveform output mode. A match sets INTFLAG.MCx on the next rising edge of CLK_TCx_CNT and can raise an interrupt, an event and a DMA request. Four waveform modes exist. In NFRQ and NPWM, TOP is PER in 8-bit mode (changed by writing PER) and fixed at MAX in 16- and 32-bit modes. NFRQ toggles WO[x] at each COUNT = CCx match, with the period set by PER or MAX. MFRQ sets the period with CC0 and toggles WO[0] at each update. NPWM is single-slope PWM: TOP sets the period and CCx the duty cycle; counting up WO[x] is set at start or at TOP and cleared at the CCx match, counting down it is cleared at start or at ZERO and set at the CCx match. MPWM drives WO[1] from CC1 with CC0 as TOP, and puts a one-clock negative pulse on WO[0] at every overflow or underflow.

operation.topic: TC double buffering and period changes
operation.text: CCx, and in 8-bit mode PER too, have buffers, each with a valid bit (CCBUFVx, PERBUFV) in STATUS. While a valid bit is 1 the matching SYNCBUSY bit is set, writing the register or its buffer gives a PAC error and access to the register is invalid. With the valid bit set and CTRLB.LUPD = 0 (written by CTRLBCLR.LUPD = 1), hardware copies the buffer at UPDATE and clears the valid bit; the software update command (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x3) works regardless of LUPD. Both registers and buffers are in the register map and buffering is optional: CTRLBSET.LUPD = 1 turns it off. In NFRQ, MFRQ or PWM counting down with buffering on, PERBUF is copied into PER continuously regardless of update conditions. A period change written to PER or CC0 takes effect after the synchronization delay. Without buffering, counting up, a new TOP below the current count makes the counter wrap round to MAX before it matches; buffering prevents this because the period changes only at the update.

Capture on channel x is enabled by CTRLA.CAPTENx. The trigger is the TC input event (enabled by EVCTRL.TCEI) or the channel's WO[x] pin, asynchronously (enabled by CTRLA.COPENx); per channel these exclude each other, though one channel can use a pin while the other uses an event. Pin capture works only in the event and time-stamp capture actions; the other actions need pin edges turned into events, and period and duty capture of a pin in PPW/PWP goes through the EIC and Event System. Event capture works in the event, PPW/PWP/PW and time-stamp actions, with the event channels asynchronous. Capture is on the rising edge by default; DRVCTRL.INVENx selects the falling edge for a pin and EVCTRL.TCINV for an event. In capture the buffer and CCx form a two-deep FIFO: once CCx has been read or is empty, CCBUFx moves into it and sets the channel flag, which can raise an interrupt, event or DMA request; CCBUFx cannot be read, so results are read from CCx. Counting up, values below 1 cannot be captured; capturing 0 needs down-counting. If a capture arrives while INTFLAG.MCx is still set, the new value is dropped and INTFLAG.ERR is set.

With EVCTRL.EVACT set to OFF, RETRIGGER, COUNT or START, the channels timestamp events or pin edges. PWP captures on both edges and restarts the counter on one, putting the period T in CC1 and the pulse width tp in CC0; PPW puts T in CC0 and tp in CC1. EVCTRL.TCINV = 1 moves the restart to the falling edge, and both channels must be in capture mode to measure both. PW captures on the falling edge, clearing and stopping the counter, and restarts counting on the rising edge; inverting the input swaps the edges. STAMP (time-stamp) copies COUNT into CCx on each capture event, or MAX after an overflow, and sets INTFLAG.MCx; TOP must be below MAX. CAPTMIN (CTRLA.CAPTMODEn) keeps the minimum value in CCx, capturing only when the count is below the last value, with CCx first set non-zero (a zero start disables capture); MCx is set when the count at an event is at or above the previous capture, marking a new local minimum. CAPTMAX keeps the maximum, capturing only when the count is above the last value, with CCx first set to something other than TOP; MCx is set when the count is at or below the previous capture, marking a new local maximum.

With CTRLBSET.ONESHOT = 1 (cleared by CTRLBCLR.ONESHOT) the counter stops at the next overflow or underflow, sets STATUS.STOP and drives the waveform outputs to zero. A retrigger command, retrigger event or start event restarts it and clears STATUS.STOP.

DMA requests: OVF, on an update (overflow, underflow or retrigger), cleared on DMA acknowledge; MCx, on each compare match (cleared on acknowledge) or when a capture is waiting in CCx (cleared when CCx is read). Interrupts OVF, MCx and ERR (capture overflow) share one request line, each with a flag in INTFLAG, enabled through INTENSET and disabled through INTENCLR. Output events OVF and MCx are enabled by EVCTRL bits (MCEOx). EVCTRL.EVACT selects one input action: OFF, START, RETRIGGER, COUNT, STAMP, PPW/PWP or PW; EVCTRL.TCEI enables the input event, which must be asynchronous.

A TC can run in any sleep mode; in Standby it needs CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1. It can wake the device by interrupt or act through events. With CTRLA.ONDEMAND = 1 it stops requesting its clock while STATUS.STOP is 1 and requests it again on a retrigger or start. Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE and STATUS.CCBUFVx, and to CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, COUNT, CCx and CCBUFx, are synchronized. Reading COUNT is synchronized on demand with the READSYNC command (CTRLBSET.CMD).

The device has five Timer/Counters for Control applications, TCC0 to TCC4; some instances have fewer channels or features (see the TCC configuration summary). Each is a counter with prescaler, up to six compare/capture channels and control logic, counting clock pulses or events. Period and compare values are double buffered and can run as circular buffers. Waveforms: frequency generation, single-slope PWM and dual-slope PWM with half-cycle reload. Capture: events, frequency and pulse width. Waveform extensions for motor control, ballast, LED, H-bridge and power converter use: an output matrix spreading channels over pins, low-side and high-side outputs with programmable dead time, swap and pattern generation (both double buffered), and dithering. Fault protection has two recoverable and two non-recoverable fault sources, the debugger being one possible non-recoverable source. Input events: two for the counter (EV0, EV1) and one per channel (MCx). Output events: count, retrigger and overflow, plus one per channel. Interrupts on overflow, retrigger, compare match or capture, and faults.

TCC pins are configured through PORT. A TCC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock source runs, its interrupts can wake the device and its events reach other peripherals without waking it. Each has a bus clock CLK_TCCx_APB gated in MCLK and needs its generic clock GCLK_TCCx set up in GCLK first; since the two clocks are asynchronous, some writes are synchronized. DMA request lines go to the DMAC and the interrupt line to the NVIC, each configured first; events go to the Event System. In debug halt it stops unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except INTFLAG, STATUS, PER, PERBUF, CCx, CCBUFx, WAVE, PATT and PATTBUF can be write-protected by the PAC. It has no analog connections.

Each TCC has up to six compare/capture channels. COUNT, PER/PERBUF and CCx/CCBUFx are 16 or 24 bits wide depending on the instance; each buffer has a valid flag (BUFV). The counter is compared with TOP and ZERO and with each CCx to raise interrupts and events and, in waveform modes, to set period and pulse width. It is driven by the prescaled GCLK_TCCx and by events, which also feed capture. The recoverable fault unit acts directly on the channel outputs from events: it can restart or halt the period, cut a pulse short or blank the output while the fault lasts, as used for current-sense regulation and zero-crossing or demagnetization retriggering; its inputs share the MCE0 and MCE1 asynchronous event sources, filtered, blanked or qualified against glitches. After the faults come, in instances that have them, the output matrix (OTMX), dead-time insertion (DTI, splitting the four lower OTMX outputs into a non-inverted low side and an inverted high side with optional dead time between), SWAP (exchanging LS and HS, for fast-decay motor control) and pattern generation (fixed levels applied at UPDATE, for stepper and full-bridge control). A non-recoverable fault forces the outputs to a preset safe level for immediate shut-down of drivers; its inputs share the count event sources TCE0 and TCE1 and, unfiltered, act asynchronously even with no clock running.

CTRLA (except RUNSTDBY, ENABLE and SWRST), FCTRLA, FCTRLB, WEXCTRL, DRVCTRL and EVCTRL are enable-protected; enable-protected CTRLA bits can be written in the same access that sets ENABLE but not one that clears it. Before enabling: turn on CLK_TCCx_APB and, for capture, set CTRLA.CPTEN for the channels. Optional settings: CTRLA.PRESCALER and CTRLA.PRESCSYNC, down-counting (CTRLBSET.DIR = 1), the waveform mode (WAVE.WAVEGEN), output polarity (WAVE.POL) and per-channel output inversion (DRVCTRL.INVEN). CTRLA.ENABLE turns the TCC on and off; CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DBGCTRL, disables the TCC, and should be used only with it disabled. The prescaler divides GCLK_TCCx by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256 or 1024; above 1, the update can happen on the next GCLK_TCCx or the next prescaled clock. Event counting bypasses the prescaler. The combined prescaler and event-action tick stream is CLK_TCCx_COUNT.

operation.topic: TCC counter operation and event actions
operation.text: Each CLK_TCCx_COUNT tick clears, reloads, increments or decrements the counter; CTRLB.DIR = 0 counts up and 1 down. Counting up it wraps from TOP to zero (overflow); counting down it reloads TOP at ZERO (underflow); either sets INTFLAG.OVF, which can raise an interrupt or event, and stops the counter in one-shot mode. When counting down, COUNT must first be set to TOP (PER or CC0). COUNT can be written while running, the write taking priority; a fresh start begins at ZERO or TOP unless COUNT was written or the TCC stopped elsewhere; the direction can change while running. STOP (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x2) holds the count, sets waveforms to the non-recoverable state given by DRVCTRL.NREx and NRVx, and sets STATUS.STOP. Pause: with EVCTRL.EVACT1 = 0x3 (STOP) an event freezes the counter and keeps the waveforms as they are until a start event (EVCTRL.EVACT0 = 0x3). RETRIGGER (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x1 or EVACTn = 0x1) clears or reloads by direction and sets INTFLAG.TRG, optionally with an event (EVCTRL.TRGEO); a stopped counter resumes from COUNT; with a retrigger action set, enabling does not start the counter, the next event does and later events restart it. START (EVACT0 = 0x3) starts a stopped counter and is ignored while counting; with it set, enabling does not start the counter and later events do not restart it. COUNT (EVACT0 = 0x5) counts events by direction. DIR (EVACT1 = 0x2), on an asynchronous path, makes the event level set the direction. INC (EVACT0 = 0x4) increments on TCE0 and DEC (EVACT1 = 0x4) decrements on TCE1 regardless of direction. FAULT (EVACTn = 0x7) stops the counter and overrides the outputs per DRVCTRL.NREx and NRVx, with TCE0 and TCE1 asynchronous. With the action OFF (0x0), enabling the counter starts it.

Channels default to compare and are reconfigured for capture. CCBUFx double buffers CCx, copied at UPDATE or on a forced update (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x3), keeping pulses symmetric and outputs glitch-free. For a waveform on a pin: choose WAVE.WAVEGEN, optionally invert WO[x] with DRVCTRL.INVENx, configure the pin in PORT; events are not used on a channel in waveform output mode. A match sets INTFLAG.MCx on the next rising edge of CLK_TCC_COUNT, and an interrupt (INTENSET.MCx) and event (EVCTRL.MCEOx) can both follow. Seven waveform modes: NFRQ, MFRQ, NPWM and the dual-slope DSTOP, DSBOTTOM, DSBOTH and DSCRITICAL. MFRQ uses CC0 as TOP, the others PER. Dual-slope modes update when the counter reaches ZERO; the others at wraparound, overflow, underflow or retrigger. NFRQ toggles WO[x] at each COUNT = CCx match with the period set by PER; MFRQ sets the period with CC0 and toggles WO[0] at each update. NPWM is single-slope PWM: TOP sets the period and CCx the duty; counting up WO[x] is set at start or at TOP and cleared at the CCx match, counting down it is cleared at start or at ZERO and set at the CCx match.

In dual-slope PWM the counter runs from ZERO up to PER and back down; WO[x] is set at the CCx match counting up and cleared at the match counting down, and interrupts or events come at TOP (counting up) and/or ZERO. DSBOTH needs the circular buffer enabled for its update at TOP. Dual-slope reaches a lower maximum frequency than single-slope; PER sets the resolution, at least 1 bit (TOP = 0x00000001), and the highest output frequency is half fGCLK_TCCx with TOP = 0x00000001 and no prescaling. In DSTOP, DSBOTTOM and DSBOTH with TOP below MAX/2, the CCx MSB chooses the ramp on which the match interrupt or event comes: rising for CCx[MSB] = 0, falling for 1. DSCRITICAL makes non-aligned centred pulses: PER sets the period, CCx places the output edge while counting up and CC(x + CC_NUM/2) the edge while counting down.

WAVE.POLx applies in every waveform mode. In single- and dual-slope PWM it flips, per channel, whether the pulse is aligned to the start or the end of the cycle. In NFRQ and MFRQ it gives the initial state of the output.

operation.topic: TCC double buffering and period changes
operation.text: PATT, PER and CCx are double buffered, each buffer with a valid bit in STATUS (PATTBUFV, PERBUFV, CCBUFVx). While a valid bit is 1 the matching SYNCBUSY bit is set, writing the register or its buffer gives a PAC error and reading the register is invalid. With the valid bit set and CTRLB.LUPD = 0 (written by CTRLBCLR.LUPD = 1), hardware copies the buffer at UPDATE and clears the valid bit; the software update command (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x3) works regardless of LUPD. Buffering is optional; writing CTRLBSET.LUPD = 1 turns it off. In NFRQ, MFRQ or PWM counting down with buffering on, PERBUF is copied into PER continuously regardless of update conditions. A new TOP written to PER or CC0 takes effect after the synchronization delay whether or not buffering is on. Without buffering, counting up, a TOP written below the current count makes the counter wrap round before it matches; with buffering the period changes only at the update, so no wraparound or odd waveform occurs.

Capture on channel x needs EVCTRL.MCEIx = 1 and CTRLA.CPTENx = 1, with asynchronous event channels. Each capture event stores a timestamp. Buffer and CCx form a two-deep FIFO: once CCx has been read or is empty, CCBUFx moves into it and sets the channel flag, which can raise an interrupt, event or DMA request; CCBUFx cannot be read. A capture arriving while STATUS.CCBUFV (or INTFLAG.MCx) is still set is dropped and INTFLAG.ERR is set. PPW and PWP (EVCTRL.EVACT1) capture on both edges and restart on one: PPW puts the period T in CC0 and pulse width tp in CC1, PWP the reverse; EVCTRL.TCEINVx = 1 moves the restart to the falling edge. A channel not in capture mode ignores the action and stays in compare, so the other can be used elsewhere. Counting up, values below 1 cannot be captured in CAPTMIN mode; capturing 0 needs down-counting. In dual-slope PWM with TOP below MAX/2, the CCx MSB records the direction at capture: 0 on a rising ramp, 1 on a falling ramp.

With CTRLBSET.ONESHOT = 1 (cleared by CTRLBCLR.ONESHOT) the counter stops at the next overflow or underflow, sets STATUS.STOP and drives the outputs to the values in DRVCTRL.NREx and NRVx; a retrigger command, retrigger event or start event restarts it and clears STATUS.STOP. PER and CC0 to CC5 can run as circular buffers: at each update the register value is copied back into its buffer. Circular buffering is meant for RAMP2, RAMP2A and DSBOTH.

Dithering adds extra clock cycles to some pulses within a frame of 16, 32 or 64 PWM cycles, improving the average pulse width or period; the extra cycles are spread one at a time by a blue-noise sequence that keeps flicker low. CTRLA.RESOLUTION selects DITH4 (16-cycle frame), DITH5 (32) or DITH6 (64). The low DITHERCY bits of COUNT, PER and CCx give the number of extra cycles per frame (in DITH4 the 4 least significant bits) and the remaining bits the value itself. An extra cycle is added in a given cycle when ((MASK AND (cycle × DITHERCY)) + DITHERCY) > MASK, with MASK = 0x0F for DITH4, 0x1F for DITH5 and 0x3F for DITH6. Dithering CCx changes the average pulse width and leaves the period unchanged.

WAVE.RAMP selects one of three ramp modes, all in single-slope PWM. RAMP1 is ordinary single-slope PWM. RAMP2 modes, for power factor correction, half-bridge and push-pull SMPS, interleave two counter cycles A and B: odd channel outputs are off in cycle A and even ones in cycle B; the ramp index changes at each update and can be changed by CTRLBSET.IDXCMD. Standard RAMP2: PER sets both ramp periods, different per ramp with the circular period buffer (WAVE.CIPEREN = 1); it uses two channels for two outputs, or one output with the other channel capturing. RAMP2A: with the circular buffers on, CC0 drives both WO[0] and WO[1] with the same polarity, and channel 1 is free to capture. RAMP2C (critical): CC0 sets the period of ramp A and PER that of ramp B, without the update constraint of circular buffers; with more than two channels WO[0] is set by CC2 and cleared by CC0, and on a two-channel TCC with WAVE.POL0 = 0 a WO[0] pulse lasts the whole of ramp A.

Two recoverable faults, A and B, act on CC0 and CC1, clamping their outputs inactive while the fault lasts or from the fault to the end of the cycle; they can also restart or halt the counter. The inputs are the first two channel input events (TCCxMC0 for A, TCCxMC1 for B), on asynchronous event channels, and the TCC must be in a PWM mode. Each input has three filters in FCTRLA/FCTRLB, usable together. Input filtering: detection is asynchronous by default and acts at once, even in power modes without a clock; FCTRLn.FILTERVAL discards events shorter than that many clock cycles and delays valid ones by the same. Blanking: FCTRLn.BLANK picks a waveform edge after which faults are ignored for FCTRLn.BLANKVAL cycles; FCTRLn.BLANKPRESC = 1 clocks blanking from fGCLK_TCCx/64 instead of fGCLK_TCCx. The longest blanking (BLANKVAL = 255) is 2.67 µs at 96 MHz without prescaling or 170 µs with it, and 170 µs or 10.9 ms at 1 MHz. Qualification (FCTRLn.QUAL = 1) ignores the fault input whenever the channel output is inactive.

Fault A and B actions are set separately and most can be combined. Keep (FCTRLn.KEEP = 1) clamps the channel output to zero while the fault lasts, releasing it at the start of the first cycle after the fault ends. Restart (FCTRLn.RESTART = 1) ends the cycle and starts a new one as soon as the fault appears; in RAMP1 the outputs stay inactive while the fault lasts, and in RAMP2 the cycle index changes and fault A counts only in cycle A, fault B only in cycle B. Capture (FCTRLn.CAPTURE) records the count at the fault: CAPT is ordinary capture with MCx set at every capture; CAPTMIN and CAPTMAX keep the smallest or largest value in CCx, capturing only a lower (or higher) count and setting MCx on a new absolute local minimum (maximum), with CCx first set away from zero (CAPTMIN) or TOP (CAPTMAX) or no capture happens; LOCMIN and LOCMAX capture every event, CCx following the count, and flag a local minimum or maximum; DERIV0 flags either (LOCMIN OR LOCMAX). In CAPT an interrupt comes on every filtered fault and capture, in the other modes only on an extreme value. Hardware halt (FCTRLn.HALT = 0x1) stops the counter and stretches the cycle while the fault lasts, the output held inactive, then resumes (or restarts, if restart is also on); in RAMP2 and RAMP2A a new cycle changes the cycle index. Software halt (FCTRLn.HALT = 0x2) is the same but resumes only once the fault has gone and software has cleared STATUS.FAULTn.

A non-recoverable fault, from the EV0 or EV1 input with EVCTRL.EVACT0 or EVACT1 set to fault, forces every compare output to the level set by DRVCTRL.NRE and NRV. DRVCTRL.FILTERVALn adds a digital filter, making detection synchronous and delaying the action by that many clock cycles. With DBGCTRL.FDDBD = 1, entering debug raises a non-recoverable debug fault state and its interrupt (DFS). In RAMP2, RAMP2A or DSBOTH, if the ramp index or direction changes while CTRLBSET.LUPD = 1, a non-recoverable update fault state and its interrupt (UFS) are raised.

With the STAMP event action, each capture event from the Event System or a pin copies COUNT into CCx, or MAX after an overflow, and sets INTFLAG.MCx; TOP must be below MAX. A capture arriving while INTFLAG.MCx is still set is dropped and INTFLAG.ERR is set.

After the recoverable fault stage, each pin pair passes through four optional units in turn: output matrix, dead-time insertion, swap and pattern generation. DTI and SWAP work in slices, slice x acting on the pins WO[x] and WO[WO_NUM/2 + x]. The output matrix routes channels to outputs per WEXCTRL.OTMX: 0x0 (default) spreads channels in order, repeating modulo the channel count; 0x1 repeats modulo half the channel count, giving the lower channels twice the outputs, for example a full bridge from two channels; 0x2 sends CC0 to every pin, for a stepper motor with pattern generation; 0x3 sends CC0 to the first output and CC1 to all others, to drive as many as seven LED strings through a boost stage.

operation.topic: TCC dead-time insertion and pattern generation
operation.text: The DTI stage has four identical generators serving channels 0 to 3, sharing one dead-time setting with separate low-side and high-side values. Each produces a non-inverted low side (LS) and an inverted high side (HS), both forced low during the dead time so they never switch together. An 8-bit counter counts down one per peripheral clock; while it is non-zero both outputs are off. A rising edge of the OTMX output reloads it from DTLS, a falling edge from DTHS. The pattern generator puts a synchronized bit pattern on its pins, for BLDC and stepper commutation and full-bridge control: PATT.PGE enables pattern control per output and PATT.PGV gives the level, each double buffered (PGEB, PGVB) and updated at UPDATE, or written directly when no synchronization is wanted.
Two or more TCCs on the same GCLK_TCCx can be linked for more synchronized channels: setting CTRLA.MSYNC in a client instance makes its channels follow the host's counter.

OVF request: with CTRLA.DMAOS = 0, one per cycle with an update (overflow, underflow or retrigger); with DMAOS = 1, one on the cycle after the DMA one-shot command (CTRLBSET.CMD = DMAOS); cleared on acknowledge. Compare match MCx: set on a match only when DMAOS = 0, cleared on acknowledge; none when DMAOS = 1. Capture MCx: set while valid data is in CCx and cleared when CCx is read, regardless of DMAOS. Circular buffers, meant for RAMP2, RAMP2A and DSBOTH only, must be refilled in order and in step with the timer, which the DMA triggers ensure. In RAMP2 and RAMP2A a circular-buffer channel's request comes at the start of ramp B rather than on a match, and with any circular buffer on the OVF request comes at the start of ramp A once the previous ramp-B transfer was acknowledged: one DMA channel on the MC trigger reloads the ramp-A values and a second on OVF the ramp-B values. In DSBOTH the channel request comes at the start of down-counting and OVF at the start of up-counting, after the previous down-counting transfer, with one DMA channel for each phase.

Interrupt sources: OVF, TRG (retrigger), CNT (see EVCTRL.CNTSEL), ERR (capture overflow), UFS (non-recoverable update fault), DFS (debug fault state), FAULTn (recoverable), FAULTx (non-recoverable) and MCx; all are asynchronous wake-up sources and share one request line, each with an INTFLAG flag enabled through INTENSET and disabled through INTENCLR. Output events OVF, TRG, CNT and MCx are enabled by EVCTRL.xxEO bits. A channel input event (MCx) captures or raises a recoverable or non-recoverable fault. EV1 actions: retrigger, direction control, stop, decrement, capture of period and pulse width, or a non-recoverable fault. EV0 actions: retrigger, count by direction, start (on the rising edge, then counting the prescaled clock to TOP or ZERO without restarting on later events), increment regardless of direction, count by direction on each prescaled clock while an asynchronous event is active, non-recoverable fault. EVCTRL.EVACT0 and EVACT1 select the actions and EVCTRL.MCEIx and TCEIx enable the inputs; with several events connected, the action applies to each. A TCC can run in any sleep mode, in Standby with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1, and can wake the device by interrupt or act through events.

Writes to CTRLA.SWRST and CTRLA.ENABLE, and to CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, STATUS, PATT, PATTBUF, WAVE, COUNT, PER, PERBUF, CCx and CCBUFx, are synchronized. Reads of CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, PATT, PATTBUF, WAVE, PER, PERBUF, CCx and CCBUFx are synchronized, and COUNT is read-synchronized on demand with the READSYNC command (CTRLBSET.CMD).

The Peripheral Touch Controller measures capacitive touch sensors (buttons, sliders, wheels) whose electrodes, usually made on the PCB, connect straight to its pins. It handles mutual-capacitance sensors, an X (transmit) pin and a Y (sense) pin per line in a matrix that can be an ITO grid, and self-capacitance sensors, one Y pin per sensor, mixed as needed; how many pins and which X and Y lines are available depends on package and configuration. Features: one pin per electrode and no external components; low power and high sensitivity; wake-up on touch from sleep; charge sensing with parasitic-capacitance compensation and adjustable gain; zero drift over temperature and VDDANA with automatic calibration and recalibration; single-shot or free-running measurement; hardware noise filtering and desynchronization for conducted immunity; selectable channel-change delay for settling; acquisition started by command or automatically; an interrupt when acquisition completes. It converts through the ADC: ADC0 is then given over to the PTC and must be enabled and configured for it. The PTC is used through the MPLAB Harmony v3 Touch Library.

X and Y pins connect to the sensor electrodes with no other parts needed; a series resistor of 1 kΩ or more on the X and Y lines improves EMC performance. A mutual-capacitance sensor is the capacitance between an X electrode that transmits and a Y electrode that senses; a matrix of n X lines and m Y lines gives sensors Cx0,y0 to Cxn,ym. A self-capacitance sensor is one Y electrode on one pin, and its capacitance Cy is measured.

The Inter-IC Sound controller is a synchronous, bidirectional digital audio link to external audio devices. It follows the I2S bus specification, and also handles TDM links to multi-slot codecs and PDM input from MEMS microphones. Inside are a pair of clock units plus a transmitter and a receiver serializer, each enabled on its own, and works as host, client or controller. Its pins are SDO, SDI, FSn, SCKn and MCKn. Each serializer has its own DMAC request, using either one DMA channel for every data channel or two channels for different data channels, so stereo codecs, stereo DACs and ADCs, multi-slot TDM devices and mono or stereo PDM microphones can be served without the CPU. 8-bit and 16-bit compact stereo put the left and right samples in one data word to halve DMA traffic. In host and controller modes MCKn can output a clock from 16×fs to 1024×fs for an external codec or DSP (for example 384×fs).

Data formats: 32-, 24-, 20-, 18-, 16- and 8-bit mono or stereo, and 16- and 8-bit compact stereo. Frame formats: two-channel I2S with word select; TDM with 1 to 8 slots, frame sync and slots enabled one by one; one- or two-channel PDM reception; one-channel burst transfer with a non-periodic frame sync. Two independent clock units drive the serializers from one clock or from separate clocks and cover sample rates including 32 kHz, 44.1 kHz, 48 kHz, 88.2 kHz, 96 kHz and 192 kHz, with a 16×fs to 1024×fs host clock. Host mode moves data on internally generated clocks and drives SCKn, MCKn and FSn; client mode moves data on external clocks at SCKn or MCKn; controller mode only outputs the generated MCKn, SCKn and FSn. Clock units and serializers are enabled separately. Data holding register management keeps slots from being mixed up after an overrun or underrun.

I2S pins are assigned to the peripheral in PORT; only the inputs and outputs in use need be enabled, and unused ones stay available as general I/O. The I2S keeps running in any sleep mode whose source clocks run. The bus clock CLK_I2S_APB comes from the power manager, is off after reset and is turned on there; the I2S should be disabled before this clock is turned off, or it can freeze in an undefined state. Two generic clocks, GCLK_I2S_0 and GCLK_I2S_1, one per clock unit, are used only in host and controller modes; each must be set up and enabled before use and before a software reset, so every clock domain resets. In host mode clock unit 0 can clock both serializers for synchronous transfers, or each serializer can take its own clock unit for unrelated clocks. DMA requests go to the DMAC and the interrupt line to the NVIC, each configured first. The I2S has no events and no analog connections. It keeps running while the CPU is halted in debug, and can be forced to halt then. All writable registers except DATAm, INTFLAG and SYNCBUSY can be write-protected by the PAC (not for an external debugger).

Transfers use SDO (transmit), SDI (receive), SCKn (serial clock of clock unit n, n = 0 or 1), FSn (frame sync or word select, marking the start of each frame) and optionally MCKn, an oversampling clock for an external codec. A frame starts on the active edge of the frame sync and holds 1 to 8 slots of 8, 16, 24 or 32 bits; each slot carries one sample of 8, 16, 18, 20, 24 or 32 bits, MSB first. The sample period is Ts = 1/fs. In mono transmit, data written for the left channel is sent on the right as well; in mono receive the right channel is ignored and the left sample is copied to the right. In mono TDM with more than two slots, each even-numbered slot is copied to the odd slot after it, in both directions. SERCTRLm.MONO = 1 selects mono. In two-channel I2S mode one or two slots are configured and successive words alternate left and right, told apart by the level of FSn; a frame holds one or two words, one slot being enough in compact stereo, and two slots possible with 32-bit slots. In TDM up to 8 slots are configured (4 slots give 4 words per frame). In PDM a 1-bit sample is on SDI at each rising and each falling edge of SCKn. Burst mode, for non-audio control data such as to a DSP, starts one transfer at each frame sync pulse, which is one bit wide and comes only when a transfer is requested; compact stereo (16C and 8C) is not available in burst mode.

The transmit serializer uses clock unit 0; the receive serializer uses clock unit 0 as well or clock unit 1. CLKCTRLn and TXCTRL and/or RXCTRL are written before the I2S is enabled, and in host mode a generic clock is set to the needed frequency: fs sets the frame period, CLKCTRLn.NBSLOTS the slots per frame, CLKCTRLn.SLOTSIZE the bits per slot. The clock units and serializers start when CTRLA.CKENn, TXEN and/or RXEN and CTRLA.ENABLE are written 1. A clock unit alone can be enabled, in controller mode, to drive MCKn, SCKn and FSn; clock units must be enabled whenever serializers are. Each can be stopped on its own by writing 0 to CKENn, TXEN or RXEN; a transmitter stops after any pending frames are sent, and a receiver after finishing the current slot.

For fs = 48 kHz with MCKn = 384×fs = 18.432 MHz, the generic clock runs at 18.432 MHz and CLKCTRLn.MCKOUTDIV = 0x0 (divide by 1). With 6 slots per frame (NBSLOTS = 0x5) of 32 bits (SLOTSIZE = 0x3), fSCKn = 48 kHz × 6 × 32 = 9.216 MHz, obtained by dividing 18.432 MHz by 2 with CLKCTRLn.MCKDIV = 0x1. Without MCKn the generic clock can be set to 9.216 MHz with MCKDIV = 0x0.

The receiver is read from RXDATA whenever INTFLAG.RXRDYm is set; successive reads give left then right samples, or slots first to last in TDM (for example four reads for a four-slot frame). The transmitter is written through TXDATA whenever INTFLAG.TXRDYm is set, in the same order. The flags can be polled in INTFLAG, raise interrupts enabled in INTENSET, or trigger DMA transfers: four DMAC trigger sources, I2S RX 0, I2S RX 1, I2S TX 0 and I2S TX 1 (named I2S_DMAC_ID_RX_m and _TX_m, m = 0 or 1), each moving one word when its ready flag is set.

In client mode an external host drives the serial clock and the frame sync (word select in I2S, frame sync in TDM): SCKn and FSn are inputs and no generic clock is needed. In host mode the I2S generates MCKn, SCKn and FSn as outputs from a generic clock, configured in CLKCTRLn; a codec may want a host clock at a multiple of fs, 256×fs for instance. Controller mode needs only the clock unit set up, through CTRLA and CLKCTRLn (dividers, slot count and size, frame sync, clock enables). In host mode CLKCTRLn.MCKEN = 1 puts GCLK_I2S_n on MCKn, divided by MCKOUTDIV + 1 (CLKCTRLn.MCKSEL and MCKOUTDIV). With CLKCTRLn.MCKSEL and SCKSEL both 0, SCKn is GCLK_I2S_n divided by MCKDIV + 1. Where no MCKn is needed, the generic clock can serve directly as SCKn with MCKDIV = 0; where the generic clock is a multiple of SCKn, MCKDIV sets the ratio. Output inversion is selectable for MCKn, SCKn and FSn (MCKOUTINV, SCKOUTINV, FSOUTINV), and FSINV inverts the frame sync. FSn is the word select in I2S format and the frame sync in TDM format.

Each serializer has one data register, TXDATA or RXDATA, used for every slot. A new word in RXDATA sets INTFLAG.RXRDYm, cleared by reading RXDATA; a word arriving before the previous one is read is an overrun and sets INTFLAG.RXORm, cleared by writing 1. An empty TXDATA sets INTFLAG.TXRDYm, cleared by writing TXDATA; if a word has gone out and none is written before the next slot, INTFLAG.TXURm marks an underrun (cleared by writing 1), and TXCTRL.TXSAME chooses whether a zero word (0) or the last word for that slot (1) is sent again.

operation.topic: I2S host, controller and client modes
operation.text: Host and controller modes supply the serial clock, the word select or frame sync and optionally the host clock. Controller mode keeps both serializers off and only the clocks are output for external transmitters and receivers. In client mode the serial clock and the word select or frame sync come from an external host, and SCKn and FSn are inputs.

In I2S format the data is left-adjusted in the word-select slot, MSB first, beginning one clock period after FSn changes. Data changes on the falling edge of SCKn and is sampled on the rising edge. FSn low marks the left channel and high the right. A 16-bit compact stereo receiver uses CLKCTRL0.SLOTSIZE = 0x1 (16 bits), CLKCTRL0.NBSLOTS = 0x1 (2 slots), RXCTRL.DATASIZE = 0x05 (16-bit compact stereo), CLKCTRLn.BITDELAY = 0x01 (one bit of delay) and CLKCTRLn.FSWIDTH = 0x01 (half frame). A 24-bit stereo transmitter in 24-bit slots uses SLOTSIZE = 0x2, NBSLOTS = 0x1, TXCTRL.DATASIZE = 0x01 (24 bits), BITDELAY = 0x01 and FSWIDTH = 0x01. Both give word select low for left and high for right; clock and DMA settings come on top. The word length, 8, 16, 18, 20, 24 or 32 bits, is set in RXCTRL.DATASIZE or TXCTRL.DATASIZE. When the slot is longer than the word, bits are added as RXCTRL/TXCTRL.EXTEND specifies; when it is shorter, the extra bits are not sent, or the received word is extended per EXTEND.

A TDM frame carries CLKCTRLn.NBSLOTS + 1 slots. CLKCTRLn.FSWIDTH sets the frame sync pulse length: a single SCKn period (BIT), a whole slot (SLOT) or half the frame (HALF), and CLKCTRLn.FSINV its polarity. RXCTRL and TXCTRL set left or right adjustment in the slot, MSB or LSB first, and whether a transfer starts on the FSn transition or one clock later (CLKCTRLn.BITDELAY). Data changes on the falling edge of SCKn and is sampled on the rising edge; FSn marks the start of slot 0. Slot count, slot size, word length (8, 16, 18, 20, 24 or 32 bits) and extension work as in I2S format.

In PDM mode a 1-bit sample from a MEMS microphone appears on SDI at each rising edge of SCKn; with two microphones the second (right channel) is set to drive its data on each falling edge. A single microphone is read in ordinary receive mode, one slot, with 16- or 32-bit words, packing 16 or 32 samples per word. Two microphones use PDM2 mode with one slot and 32-bit data: 16 samples of each are packed into one word, left in the lower half and right in the upper half, as in compact stereo; PDM2 is set with SLOTSIZE = 0x01 (16 bits), NBSLOTS = 0x00 (1 slot) and RXCTRL.DATASIZE = 0x00 (32 bits). SCKn is set by GCLK_I2S_n and CLKCTRLn.MCKDIV to the microphone's oversampling frequency: fs = 48 kHz with fo = 64 × fs needs SCKn = 3.072 MHz. Only the SCKn and SDI pins are used.

Received words pass through a formatting unit before reaching the data holding register, and written words through another before transmission. RXCTRL and TXCTRL select SLOTADJ (justify left or right within the slot), BITREV (reverse bit order), WORDADJ (justify left or right within the data word) and EXTEND (how the word is extended to the word size).

RXCTRL/TXCTRL.DMA connects a serializer to one DMAC channel, or in stereo to one channel per slot. The DMAC reads RXDATA and writes TXDATA for each slot in turn, with 32-, 16- or 8-bit transfers following DATASIZE; 8-bit compact stereo uses 16-bit transfers and 16-bit compact stereo 32-bit transfers.

Interrupt sources are RXRDYm (receive ready), RXORm (receive overrun), TXRDYm (transmit ready) and TXURm (transmit underrun); all are asynchronous and wake the device from any sleep mode. Each has a flag in INTFLAG, is enabled in INTENSET and disabled in INTENCLR; a request stays active until the flag is cleared, the source disabled or the I2S reset. All sources share one NVIC line, so INTFLAG is read to find the cause, and interrupts must be enabled globally. The I2S has no events. It runs in every sleep mode that keeps its clocks.

Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLA.CKENx, CTRLA.TXEN and CTRLA.RXEN are synchronized, each setting its SYNCBUSY bit until done. TXDATA is write-synchronized (SYNCBUSY.TXDATA) and RXDATA read-synchronized (SYNCBUSY.RXDATA). Starting a synchronized operation while its SYNCBUSY bit is 1 causes a peripheral bus error.

For debugging, RXCTRL.RXLOOP = 1 connects SDO to SDI inside the I2S so transmitted data is received; RXLOOP = 0 restores the SDI pin. The receive serializer must be disabled before this setting is changed.
