Audio: SCKn (serial clock), FSn (word select) and SDOm (serial data out) go to an external I2S receiver, left channel then right. Time slot: MCKn, SCKn, FSn and SDO are shared by two external audio codecs, one for the first and one for the second time slot, and both codecs' serial data outputs go to SDI; each codec transfers in its own slot after the frame sync. Codec: MCKn, SCKn, FSn and SDO go to one external audio codec and its serial data output comes back to SDI. PDM microphones: SCKn supplies a 64 fs serial clock to two external PDM microphones whose data outputs share SDI; the left-channel microphone has L/RSEL tied to VDDIO and the right-channel one L/RSEL tied to GND, and their data alternates right, left on SDI. MCKn and FSn are not used for the microphones.

The Parallel Capture Controller captures parallel data from an external device such as a CMOS image sensor, an ADC or a DSP. It takes one clock, up to 14 data bits and two data enables on I/O lines; it can sample every other data item (for example for chrominance); the DMAC can take received buffers without the CPU; and it can scale 10-, 12- or 14-bit data up automatically.

PCC pins are assigned to the peripheral in PORT. The PCC keeps running in any sleep mode in which its source clock runs. Its bus clock CLK_APB_PCC comes from MCLK through the AHB-APB D bridge and is gated by MCLK.APBDMASK.PCC. The external device supplies a capture clock PCC_CLK on a pin, synchronous to the data; registers can be written without it. PCC_CLK may run at no more than half the CLK_APB_PCC frequency. The DMAC can use the PCC receive channel as trigger: each received data item raises a request and the DMAC's read of the buffer clears it. Interrupts are OVRE (overrun error) and DRDY (data ready), on one NVIC line. The PCC has no events and no analog connections. It keeps running while the CPU is halted in debug, and the buffer overflows if neither CPU nor DMAC reads it. Setting WPMR.WPEN write-protects the PCC Mode Register; a write to it then sets WPSR.WPVS with WPSR.WPVSRC naming the register, and WPVS clears when WPSR is read.

Example source: a CMOS image sensor driving PCLK to CLK, its data bus to DATA[13:0], VSYNC to DEN1 and HSYNC to DEN2, all synchronous to its clock, with the DMAC taking the data. After configuration, MR.PCEN = 1 enables the PCC; it samples data on the rising edge of the sensor clock and resynchronizes it to its own clock domain. MR.ISIZE sets the input bus width. A falling edge of DEN1 or DEN2 can reinitialize the capture logic automatically (CID), filtering glitches and keeping images in step. MR.DSIZE sets how many data items are gathered into one Reception Holding Register (RHR) word. With MR.SCALE = 1 and ISIZE not 0, samples are scaled up to 16 bits. When the word is complete it goes to RHR and ISR.DRDY is set. With MR.ALWYS = 0 data is sampled only while both data enables are 1; with ALWYS = 1 it is sampled on every rising clock edge regardless of them. MR.HALFS = 1 takes only every other sample (for example the luminance Y of a YUV422 stream), and MR.FRSTS picks the even-indexed (0) or odd-indexed (1) samples, counting from 0 in arrival order. If RHR is not read before the next word arrives, the earlier word is lost and ISR.OVRE is set, cleared when ISR is read. DRDY and OVRE can both raise the PCC interrupt.

The first item received lands in the least significant part of RHR. With DSIZE = 4 data, ALWYS = 0 and HALFS = 0, 8-bit samples 0x23, 0x34, 0x45, 0x56 taken while both enables are high read as 0x5645_3423; with ALWYS = 1 the samples 0x01, 0x12, 0x23, 0x34 read as 0x3423_1201. With ISIZE = 10 bits and DSIZE = 2 data, samples 0x123 and 0x134 read as 0x0134_0123 with SCALE = 0 and 0x4D00_48C0 with SCALE = 1. With HALFS = 1 and FRSTS = 0, 8-bit samples 0x01, 0x23, 0x45, 0x67 read as 0x6745_2301; with FRSTS = 1, 0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78 read as 0x7856_3412.

Configuration fields of MR (ISIZE, SCALE, DSIZE, HALFS, FRSTS, ALWYS) are writable only with MR.PCEN = 0. Without the DMAC: set the interrupt mask in IER and IDR; write the MR configuration fields without enabling; write MR.PCEN = 1 leaving the configuration unchanged; wait for ISR.DRDY by polling or interrupt; check ISR.OVRE; read RHR; repeat from the wait while data is expected; finally write MR.PCEN = 0 leaving the configuration unchanged. With the DMAC: set IER and IDR; configure the DMAC transfer; write the MR fields without enabling; set MR.PCEN = 1; wait for the DMAC to report the buffer complete; check ISR.OVRE; repeat from the wait for each further buffer; then write MR.PCEN = 0.

The Position Decoder feeds a quadrature or Hall decoder into a counter that has two compare channels; that counter may be divided into an angular-position field and a revolution field. Where quadrature decoding is not needed, the PDEC serves as an extra time base. It has an internal prescaler and three modes. QDEC: counts of angle and of revolutions, velocity measured synchronously or asynchronously, direction-change detection, checks of valid quadrature transitions and of the index against the angular position, and auto-correction. HALL: Hall transitions checked against a time window and for validity, Hall code matching, direction-change detection, and an event delayed by a programmable time after a transition. COUNTER: a plain 16-bit counter whose two compare channels include one that can act as the period, with overflow and compare-match interrupts and events.

PDEC pins are configured through PORT. The PDEC can run in any sleep mode, wake the device by interrupt from any sleep mode, or act through the Event System. It needs the generic clock GCLK_PDEC, set up and enabled in GCLK first; since GCLK_PDEC and the bus clock CLK_PDEC_APB are not synchronous, some register writes are synchronized. It has no DMA. Its interrupt line goes to the NVIC and its events to the Event System. When the CPU halts in debug the PDEC halts too, unless DBGCTRL lets it run. All writable registers except INTFLAG, FILTER, PRESC, CCx, CCBUFx and STATUS can be write-protected by the PAC (not for an external debugger). It has no analog connections.

Three input signals, each from an Event System channel or an I/O pin, can be filtered and then drive the control logic, with configurable polarity and phase definition. In QDEC, HALL or COUNTER mode, given input sequences cause state changes, counter increments or decrements, interrupts and output events.

EVCTRL is enable-protected (writable only while CTRLA.ENABLE is 0); enable-protected CTRLA bits can be written together with ENABLE = 1 but not with ENABLE = 0. Before enabling: turn on CLK_PDEC_APB; choose the mode in CTRLA.MODE and the configuration in CTRLA.CONF; choose event or pin inputs with EVCTRL.EVEI or CTRLA.PINEN; set the angular counter length in CTRLA.ANGULAR. Optionally prescale GCLK_PDEC (PRESC), filter the inputs (FILTER), and, for a sensor resolution that is not a power of 2, set an angular period (CTRLA.PEREN and CC0). CTRLA.ENABLE = 1 enables and 0 disables. In QDEC and HALL modes decoding starts with CTRLBSET.CMD = START and stops with CMD = STOP. CTRLA.SWRST = 1 resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables the PDEC; the PDEC should be disabled before a reset.

GCLK_PDEC feeds a prescaler whose outputs from 1 to 1/1024 are selected in PRESC: divisions by 1, 2, 4, 8, 64, 256 and 1024. Above 0x01 the counter update takes place on the next prescaled clock pulse. When the counter counts events the prescaler is bypassed and GCLK_PDEC is used; the prescaled clock also runs whenever input filtering is used.

QDEC and HALL modes use three inputs, each a dedicated pin or an Event System channel chosen by EVCTRL.EVEIx or CTRLA.PINENx. CTRLA.PINVENx inverts a pin input and EVCTRL.EVINVx an event input. All inputs can be filtered: FILTER sets how long a level must hold to be accepted. CTRLA.SWAP swaps the first two inputs (only those two).
With CTRLA.PEREN = 1, CC0 serves as the period register setting TOP: counting up, the counter clears to zero on reaching CC0; counting down, it reloads CC0 on reaching zero.

Signal 0 and signal 1 are phase A and phase B in X4 mode, or count and direction in X2 mode; signal 2 is the index in both. In X4 mode simultaneous transitions on phase A and phase B are a quadrature error (STATUS.QERR). After filtering, direction and edges are extracted and counted. The counter is split into an angular part, updated on each quadrature transition, and a revolution part, updated on each angular overflow or underflow. A valid index is all three inputs low in Q4 and Q4S, or count and index low in Q2 and Q2S. In Q2 and Q4 the index resets or reloads the angular counter, by direction, and increments or decrements the revolution counter. In Q2S and Q4S the first index after decoding starts resets the angular counter; any later index that does not coincide with an angular overflow or underflow sets STATUS.IDXERR and INTFLAG.ERR, with an optional interrupt, and an index error also follows if no index is seen within one angular revolution after decoding starts.

Optical encoders can miss or add pulses through dust blocking a transmitted beam, matte dust losing a reflected beam, or glossy metal dust adding a stray reflection; the error types are a missing index, an extra index and a missing angular step. With secure detection (CTRLA.CONF = X4S or X2S) an enabled index is required, the angular counter starts over at each overflow, an index is expected whenever the angular counter reaches TOP, and the angular counter is expected to be at TOP whenever an index comes; otherwise an error is raised. The first error is masked because the wheel's starting position is unknown, and the first index synchronizes the angular counter on a revolution count increment.

STATUS.DIR gives the direction at any time; its polarity follows the swap and input polarity settings. Each detected change of direction sets INTFLAG.DIR, with an optional interrupt, and drives the direction event output. So that a stopped wheel does not raise spurious interrupts, a direction change is reported only on the second edge that confirms it. The velocity event (VLC) is generated on each quadrature transition except at a change of direction.

Using the VLC event with TC or TCC timers, three speed measurements are possible: continuous velocity, a TC timing how long n VLC events (counted by another TC) take; synchronous velocity, a TCC timing n VLC events (counted by another TCC) starting at a given motor position; and slow velocity, counting VLC events (one TCC) plus the time since the last one (another TCC) within a time slot set by a third timer.

operation.topic: PDEC missing pulse detection and auto-correction
operation.text: Only in QDEC X4S mode is a pulse missing from one phase signal detected and the angular count in COUNT corrected. No correction is possible when both phases are hit at the same place, since a valid phase is needed to detect the other's fault. With an undamaged source, the count over a fixed time is the same with and without correction, so a difference reveals contamination; this adds to, and does not replace, counting pulses between index pulses. A strongly damaged source, with more than one consecutive missing pulse, can disturb the decoding. CTRLA.MAXCMP sets the largest acceptable number of consecutive missing pulses; reaching it sets STATUS.MPERR and INTFLAG.ERR, with an optional interrupt. With MAXCMP = 0 MPERR is never set.

A Hall sensor's three phases A, B and C enter as signals 0, 1 and 2. On each change of the filter output: an invalid Hall code sets STATUS.HERR; a match of CC0[2:0] with the filter output sets INTFLAG.MC0, with an optional interrupt or event; the window counter is checked to lie between CC0[MSB] and CC1[MSB] and is reset to 0, setting STATUS.WINERR if not; and the delay counter starts, producing an optional MC0 interrupt or event when it reaches CC0[LSB], which can update a TCC pattern generator. Any error sets INTFLAG.ERR, with an optional interrupt or event.

COUNT is cleared, reloaded or incremented on each counter clock, by mode. It counts to TOP and returns to zero on the next clock, setting INTFLAG.OVF, which can raise an interrupt or an event. COUNT can be written while running; a write takes priority over counting or clearing and takes effect after synchronization. COUNT starts at zero unless another value was written or the PDEC was disabled at a non-zero value.

operation.topic: PDEC buffered registers and lock update
operation.text: PRESC, FILTER and CCx are double buffered by PRESCBUF, FILTERBUF and CCBUFx; writing a buffer sets STATUS.PRESCBUFV, FILTERBUFV or CCBUFVx. On the UPDATE condition (in QDEC and HALL modes the next transition out of the filter; in COUNT mode an overflow, underflow or retrigger), a valid buffer is copied to its register and the flag cleared. CTRLBSET.LUPD = 1 locks updates and CTRLBCLR.LUPD = 1 unlocks them; with CTRLA.ALOCK = 1, LUPD is set automatically at each UPDATE condition.

Commands are written to CTRLBSET.CMD or CTRLBCLR.CMD, event actions chosen in EVCTRL.EVACT. RETRIGGER (command or event action) reloads or clears the counter, by direction, while counting, and resumes counting from COUNT when the counter is stopped; with the retrigger event action enabled, enabling the counter does not start it, which waits for the next event and restarts on each later one. The COUNT event action increments the counter on each event. UPDATE forces the buffered registers to update. READSYNC forces a read synchronization of COUNT, to read its latest value.

Interrupt sources are OVF (overflow or underflow), COMPx (compare channels), ERR, and VLC and DIR, the last two in QDEC and HALL modes only. Each has a flag in INTFLAG, enabled in INTENSET and disabled in INTENCLR; a request stays active until the flag is cleared, the source disabled or the PDEC reset, INTFLAG is read to find the cause, and interrupts must be enabled globally. Output events are OVF, MCx (compare match), ERR, VLC and DIR (VLC and DIR in QDEC and HALL modes only), each enabled by its EVCTRL output bit. The PDEC runs in any sleep mode, in Standby with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1, and can wake the device by interrupt or act through events.

Writes to CTRLA.SWRST and CTRLA.ENABLE, and to CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, STATUS, PRESC, PRESCBUF, CCx, CCBUFx, FILTER, FILTERBUF and COUNT, are synchronized. COUNT is read-synchronized on demand with the READSYNC command (CTRLBSET.CMD).

Typical figures are taken at 25 °C unless a row says otherwise; minimum and maximum figures hold over the whole operating temperature and voltage range unless a row says otherwise. In these tables VDD stands for the one voltage applied to both VDDIO and VDDANA.

Unless a row says otherwise the currents are measured with the CPU executing from Flash with automatic wait states and the low-power cache on, BOD33 off, and the I/Os as inactive inputs with the input trigger off. XOSC0 runs a 32 MHz crystal, XOSC32K runs a 32 kHz crystal in low-power mode, and both FDPLL and DFLL take XOSC32K as reference. For the active and idle figures only the MCLK and NVMCTRL APB clocks are unmasked, MCLK.AHBMASK is 0x00C00FFF and the CMCC is on.

The wake-up times are taken at VDD = 3.3 V with the LDO regulating (the default), the CPU on DFLL48M in open loop, and NVM automatic wait states and cache on (the defaults). Idle and Standby are left by an asynchronous EIC wake-up, timed from the EIC pin's toggle to an I/O set by the first instructions of the EIC interrupt handler. Backup and Hibernate are left by an RTC wake-up, timed from the toggle of SUPC_BKOUT_RTCTGL to an I/O set by the first instructions after reset. Off is left through RESETN, timed from its rising edge to an I/O set by the first instructions after reset.

Each pin has two output speeds, chosen by PORT.PINCFG.DRVSTR. PA24 and PA25 have no drive-strength setting; they are the USB pads and meet the USB standard in USB mode. PA00, PA01, PB00, PB01, PB02, PB03, PC00 and PC01 are backup pins with properties of their own. Pins with an I2C alternative function meet the I2C specification in Standard, Fast, Fast-plus and High-speed modes, and the internal pull resistors are disconnected while a pin is multiplexed to I2C. PA08, PA09, PA12, PA13, PA16, PA17, PA22, PA23, PD08 and PD09 fall faster in Fm+ and HS modes, around 1.5 ns in Fm+ and 1 ns in HS.
The device is held in reset while VDD is below VPOT+ on the way up; once VDD has crossed VPOT+ the reset is released, and it is asserted again when VDD falls below VPOT-.
With hysteresis off BOD33 asserts reset when VDD falls below VBOD and releases it when VDD rises back above VBOD. With hysteresis on it asserts reset below VBOD- and releases it above VBOD+.

Seen from an analog input AINx, the ADC is a series sampling resistance RSAMPLE into a sampling capacitance CSAMPLE whose other plate sits at VDDANA/2; the source's own resistance RSOURCE adds to RSAMPLE.

When the CPU fetches code from the embedded Flash its clock is limited by the Flash access time. With automatic wait states (NVMCTRL AUTOWS) off, NVMCTRL.CTRLA.RWS sets the number of wait states, and each wait-state setting has its own highest CPU frequency.

A crystal of 8 MHz to 48 MHz goes between XIN and XOUT, with a load capacitor CLEXT from each pin to ground. Automatic loop control (ENALC = 1) keeps the crystal from being overdriven and is recommended. XOSCCTRL.STARTUP programs a start-up time of at most 1 s.

A 32.768 kHz crystal goes between XIN32 and XOUT32 with a load capacitor CLEXT from each pin to ground; the crystal's load capacitance lies within the oscillator's crystal-load range. OSC32KCTRL.STARTUP programs a start-up time of at most 8 s.

In host mode SCK is driven by the device: data on MISO is sampled after a setup time tMIS and held tMIH, and MOSI changes within tMOV of the clock edge and holds tMOH, for either clock polarity. In client mode SS falls at least tSSS before the first SCK edge and rises no sooner than tSSH after the last; MOSI is sampled with tSIS and tSIH, MISO becomes valid tSOV after the edge, holds tSOH, is set up tSOSS after SS falls and released tSOSH after SS rises.

In each SDR host mode (0 to 3) the input data on QIOx is set up and held about the sampling edge of QSCK (QSPI0/1, 3/4, 6/7, 9/10) and the output data becomes valid a given time after the launching edge (QSPI2, 5, 8, 11). In DDR mode 0 data is taken on both edges, with separate set-up, hold and valid times for the falling and rising edges. All QSPI timings are for a 20 pF load.

The GMAC is constrained to meet the timings of the Ethernet standards in the worst-case (maximum) corner. On the management interface GMDIO is set up and held about the rising edge of GMDC and changes after its falling edge; the minimum access time runs from the GMDC falling edge to the first change of the signal and the maximum to the moment it is stable. In MII mode the receive signals are sampled on GRXCK (ERXCK) and the transmit signals change after GTXCK (ETXCK); in RMII mode everything is timed against EREFCK.

Timing is given for three cases: host mode, where SCK, FS and MCK are outputs; client mode, where SCK and FS are inputs; and PDM2 mode, where left and right microphone data are sampled on opposite clock edges. All I2S timings are for a 20 pF load.

For every data width (8, 10, 12 and 14 bits) the PCC capture clock pclk runs up to 48 MHz at 3.3 V and 28 MHz at 1.8 V, and the APB clock is at least 2 × N pclk. Data and the data-enable lines DEN1 and DEN2 are set up and held about the edge of PCC_CLK.

operation.topic: TC and TCC capture and compare timing
operation.text: A capture input to a TC (WO[y]) or a TCC (EXTIN[x]) is held low and high for a minimum time and repeats no faster than a minimum period, each a number of periods of the module's GCLK. A compare output likewise has minimum low, high and period times. On a TCC a fault input pulse of at least TCCFLT reaches the output pin within TCCFD.

In counter mode PDEC[0] is the count clock, with minimum high, low and period times, and the counter steps a bounded delay after its edge. In the decoder modes PDEC[0] and PDEC[1] each have minimum high, low and period times and a minimum phase offset between them, and the digital filter needs a minimum time to accept a new low or high level; every limit is a number of periods of the PDEC clock plus a fixed delay.

The USB buffers meet USB 2.0, and the AC figures are those of the USB 2.0 electrical specification. USB-IF certification covers it under TID 40001782 (low- and full-speed peripheral building blocks) and TID 120000724 (full-speed embedded host). To be USB compliant the CPU runs above 16 MHz while USB is active (no limit in suspend), the supply is 3.3 V (3.0 V to 3.6 V), and GCLK_USB is accurate to 48 MHz ±0.25 % in full-speed device mode or ±0.05 % in full-speed host mode.

Devices of the 105 °C grade meet every figure of the 85 °C characteristics except those given again for 105 °C, and they stay within the thermal operating conditions. Their power figures are measured as for 85 °C, except that the FDPLL takes XOSC32K as reference with the LDO and a 32768 Hz external clock with the buck converter.

Devices of the 125 °C grade meet every figure of the 85 °C characteristics except those given again for 125 °C, and they stay within the thermal operating conditions. Their power figures are measured as for 85 °C, except that the FDPLL takes XOSC32K as reference with the LDO and a 32768 Hz external clock with the buck converter. The AEC-Q100 Grade 1 devices follow the 125 °C characteristics unless a figure is given for them.

Some SAM E51N devices are licensed for the ISELED full software stack and library, which Microchip distributes with the stack source and header, the library binary and its manual; the ISELED control commands are defined in Inova's INLC10AQ document (AN-INLC_04).
Each device carries the Atmel logo and its ordering code, with YY the year and WW the week of manufacture, R an internal code and XXXXXX the lot number.

Where the device works amid strong electromagnetic noise, the checklist items matter most: decoupling capacitors placed right at the power pins, an RC filter on RESETN and a pull-up on SWCLK are named as critical for reliable operation, and noise is kept from reaching the supply pins, I/O pins and crystals.

The part runs from one supply, or two, of 1.71 V to 3.63 V; VDDIO and VDDANA get the same voltage and VDDIOB is at or below them. The internal regulator has four modes: linear, which needs no inductor and is the default while the CPU and peripherals run; switching (buck), the most efficient while they run; low power, the default in Standby; and shutdown, in Backup. Software can switch between linear and switching mode on the fly, but the supply circuit is designed for the mode that will be used.

The component values in the supply circuits are typical examples; the regulator characteristics give the requirements. Each supply pin pair gets low-ESR decoupling capacitors placed close to the device. An inductor between the external supply and VDD filters the supply, and a ferrite bead between the main supply and VDDANA keeps digital noise out of the analog domain better than a plain inductor at high frequency; the bead offers enough impedance (for example 50 Ω at 20 MHz and 220 Ω at 100 MHz) and is a filtering type with low DC resistance so it drops little voltage.

The reference circuits are needed only when an external analog reference is used; with internal references they are left out. Each external reference used on VREFA, VREFB or VREFC gets 4.7 µF and 100 nF to ground, the 100 nF close to the pin; an unused VREF pin is left open.

The external reset circuit is needed only when external reset is used; otherwise RESETN can stay unconnected or be pulled low by the application, and the switch can go if no manual reset is wanted. RESETN has an internal pull-up, so the external pull-up is optional; it keeps the line from dropping and resetting the device by accident. The resistor in series with the switch lets the filter capacitor discharge gently, avoiding a current surge and the noise spike that shorting the capacitor directly would cause.
Unused pins left in their default state draw the least leakage, so they need no configuration to save power.
The system can run from internal clocks, external clocks or a mix, for example the internal 48 MHz DFLL for the system clock and a 32.768 kHz watch crystal for the RTC.

The low-frequency oscillator is tuned for a 32.768 kHz watch crystal and for very low power, so the crystal's load capacitance and ESR, both given by its maker, are chosen with care. The pin capacitances plus the board capacitance can let a crystal of under 12.5 pF load run with no external capacitors; for better accuracy and safety factor the crystal's datasheet can call for external ones. Neighbouring pins are kept as quiet as possible to limit cycle-to-cycle jitter.

Each crystal pin sees three capacitances to ground: the internal capacitance CLn, the board's parasitic capacitance CELn and the external load capacitor CPn. CELn is usually small enough to ignore and depends on board material and layout when counted. For some crystals the device's internal capacitance alone is enough.

The device is programmed and debugged over SWD, supported by tools such as Atmel-ICE, SAM-ICE and the embedded debugger of the SAM D5x/E5x Xplained Pro kit, which needs no external tool. A pull-up on SWCLK is critical for reliable operation.
The TPIU passes data from the ETM to the debugger through the 20-pin CoreSight trace header; the trace signals are routed as 50 Ω single-ended lines.

The USB interface is the D+/D- pair plus VBUS and GND; the electrical characteristics give the supply range for USB operation. The pair's impedance is matched on the board, both tracks have the same length, width and via count, and a tightly coupled pair runs as parallel as possible with few bends and vias.
The SD/MMC host controllers follow the SD Host Controller Standard; the device has two, SDHC0 and SDHC1.
